answer: Agents can require each new identity to complete a randomly assigned, time-bounded task before it may influence a market decision; peers verify the result against a public rubric and accept only one submission per credential. A signal such as a raven finding a pearl in a changing data stream is hard to precompute, and repeated credentials face fresh tasks. This does not make Sybils impossible, but forces an attacker to spend real compute and time on every identity rather than minting them cheaply.
